howDoI.q: How do I make a block that hurts when touched?
How do I make a hazard hurt only once?
How do I make a pool or a pit that costs a life?
How do I choose where my hero starts again after he falls?
How do I give my hero a safe path over a hazard?
How do I put a bridge over a pool?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Watch Your Step is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has three short levels about things that hurt, and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each hazard is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

pages.head: Level 1: Spikes
pages.html:
Level 1: Spikes

The SPIKES HURT sign stands before a single spike. Walk into it and it stings: you lose 10 of your 50 hit points, the hero shows his hurt pose, and the spike lies flat, harmless, for the rest of the level. The JUMP OVER THEM sign stands before two more. Jump, and you lose nothing. Walk into them instead and each one stings once.

It takes five stings to lose a life, so there is room to try it. Coins are worth ten points each. There are four, and they float where only a jump reaches.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • A block that hurts. Open step.bbl in the blocks editor and pick spikeUp. Its Hit points is −10. The engine adds that to the hero on every tick that the block overlaps him, not once per touch. A block that only hurts would take all his hit points in a second.
  • Hurt once. The same block has Becomes block set to spikeFlat. The moment the hero touches a spike, the engine swaps that one block on the map for a flat, harmless one, with no hit points. One touch, one sting. This is the same rule a coin uses to disappear when you take it.
  • Nothing holds him. The spike is not solid, and it pulls down like air. The hero walks through it while it hurts and nothing keeps him inside to be hurt again. A solid block that hurt without turning into something else could trap him in a hurt that never ends.
  • You see it. The hero's Hurt sequence plays, with its sound, each time his hit points drop. Open hero.chr in the character editor. He starts with 50 hit points and 3 lives.
  • Where they are. Open one.map in the map editor. A single spike block sits on the grass, and two more side by side further along, one block high. They are ordinary blocks you paint like grass.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures. Change the words in the blocks editor and play again.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door at the end to the next level. Open step.gam in the scenes editor and look at the links of the Spikes scene.

pages.head: Level 2: The Pool
pages.html:
Level 2: The Pool

You come out of level 1 into a short room. The FALL IN AND YOU START THIS ROOM AGAIN sign stands before a pool in the ground, three blocks wide. Walk in. The hero falls over, you lose a life, and the room starts again: you are back at the doorway where you came in, with all 50 hit points, and the coins are back too. Press F2 to see that you have one life fewer.

Then jump across. There are three coins above the pool, and the exit is on the far side.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • A hazard that costs a life. Open step.bbl and pick waterTop or water. Their Hit points is −200, far more than the hero's 50. Game-Maker has no block that takes a life directly: a life is spent when the hero's hit points reach zero. A big enough hurt does that in one touch. Any number above his hit points will do.
  • Not solid. The pool has no solid sides and pulls down like air, so he drops straight in and touches it.
  • Where he comes back. When a life is lost, the game starts the same level again with one life fewer and his hit points full. He stands where he arrived the first time: the block that the link from level 1 put him on. Open two.map in the map editor. The cyan marker on the doorway is that spot. Drag it, and every fall brings him back somewhere else.
  • What starts over. The map is read from its file again, so a coin you took is back. Your score stays. With no lives left, the game ends instead.
  • Keep the room short. This room is only 24 blocks wide, so starting it again costs a few seconds, not a minute. A long level with a pool near its end would punish the player most for a small mistake. Put a hazard that costs a life in a short room.
  • The pool. In two.map it is three blocks wide and two deep, cut out of the grass and dirt. The top row is waterTop, with the waves, and the row under it is water. The dirt under that stops anything from falling off the world.

pages.head: Level 3: The Safe Way
pages.html:
Level 3: The Safe Way

The FIND A SAFE WAY ACROSS sign stands before a row of spikes and a pool. Neither is in your way if you look up and across. A row of planks hangs over the spikes: jump up through it from the side, and walk along the top. Further on, a plank bridge lies across the pool, level with the grass. Walk over it.

There are three coins on the planks. This level costs nothing if you take the safe way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 3 is made

  • Planks. The plank block is solid on its top side only, so the hero can jump up through it from below and stand on it. In three.map a row of five planks sits two blocks above the grass, over three spikes. Standing on a plank he is above the spikes, and a block only touches the hero if it overlaps him.
  • The bridge. Four planks take the place of the grass on top of the pool, with waterTop and water under them. The hero walks across on the planks and never overlaps the pool. Fall off the end, though, and you are in it.
  • A safe path is a choice. The hazards are the same blocks as in levels 1 and 2. The level just gives the hero somewhere else to go. A hazard is only fair if the player can see what to do about it, so each one has its way round in view from the start.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Make spikeUp take 25 hit points instead of 10, so two stings cost a life.
  • Make a spike hurt every time: set its Becomes block to its own number. Walk into it and watch what happens in a second.
  • Change waterTop and water to −20, so the pool is only a splash.
  • Drag the cyan marker on the doorway in two.map to move where the hero comes back.
  • Give the hero 5 lives in hero.chr.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
